entries.title: The Cisco IOS driver says why it could not connect
entries.description: A refused connection, a privilege level that could not be reached and an SSH algorithm the device does not share are raised as `HostUnreachable`, `PrivilegeFailed` and `SshAlgorithmMismatch` instead of the raw scrapli, asyncssh or socket error, so the collection agent can tell the reasons apart.

entries.title: Cisco IOS (classic) configuration starts with the spanning tree mode
entries.description: The rendered configuration now begins with `spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst` and `spanning-tree extend system-id`, as it did in earlier versions of the driver, so a switch configured from ACEX does not fall back to PVST. A `SpanningTreeGlobal` whose `mode` is `pvst`, `rapid-pvst` or `mst` (`mstp` and `rapid_pvst` are read the same way) is written as that mode instead. The lines are written but not read back from the running configuration.

entries.title: Cisco IOS (classic) writes and reads the clock timezone
entries.description: The timezone of `system.clock.config`, for example `CET 1`, is written as `clock timezone CET 1` and read from the running configuration. IOS reports the minutes as well (`CET 1 0`); a zero is left out so the device and the declared value compare equal. An offset with real minutes, such as `IST 5 30`, is kept.

entries.title: Older devices that only offer CBC ciphers over SSH can be reached
entries.description: The driver now accepts the CBC ciphers (3DES and AES) that some older devices offer over SSH. Collection and jobs against such a device used to fail with "No matching encryption algorithm found". A device that supports a modern cipher still gets one, since the CBC ciphers are only a fallback.

entries.title: The hardware model of a Cisco 1900, 2900 or 3900 router is read from the device
entries.description: These routers print their model right after "Cisco" and have no processor on that line (`Cisco CISCO1941/K9 (revision 1.0) with ...`), so the driver reported no hardware model for them. It now reads it, for example `CISCO1941/K9`, together with the serial number, OS and version.

entries.title: A driver for Cisco IOS devices
entries.description:
Devices that run classic IOS, `cisco_ios` in the inventory, have a driver of their own, Cisco IOS (classic) CLI, next to the IOS-XE driver, which is unchanged. It reads configuration that IOS prints in its own way instead of leaving it as unparsed lines: ACL entries without sequence numbers, `access-list` lines with a number, `spanning-tree portfast edge`, `ip device tracking`, and the AAA lines `aaa authorization config-commands` and `console` and `aaa accounting send stop-record` and `update newinfo`. On the IOS configurations we have measured, 57 % of the lines are read, against 41 % with the IOS-XE driver.

An asset uses the driver when its driver (NED id) is set to `CiscoIOSClassicCLIDriver`. What the driver writes to an IOS device has not been tried on a real device yet.
